g1-implement.title: G1 characterize-and-pin: prove the measuring instrument BEFORE the code moves (no source change)
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. TASK: add characterization + pinning coverage for the two-axis grouping in src/physics/instrument_panel/replication.py, and build the exact-bit snapshot harness -- WITHOUT modifying replication.py (that is G2's job; this gate's whole point is that the instrument is validated against the UNCHANGED code). Deliverables: (1) tests appended to tests/unit/physics/instrument_panel/test_replication_channel.py covering the axis-grouping contract of `_axis_means` and `main_effect_margin_uncertainty` -- balanced grid, RAGGED grid (a driver missing a class), EMPTY grid (grand mean is 0.0, dicts empty -- pin the existing semantics, do not 'fix' them), single-cell grid (driver_se/class_se are None, never 0.0), duplicate values, per-key VALUE ORDER (values accumulate in grid.items() order) and KEY INSERTION ORDER of the returned driver_mean/class_mean dicts; (2) ONE naive-accumulation pinning test built on a grid whose driver row is [1e16, 1.0, -1e16, 1.0] -- naive sequential accumulation gives 1.0, CPython>=3.12 compensated builtins.sum gives 2.0 -- asserting the module's driver mean equals the NAIVE value EXACTLY (`==` or float.hex(), never pytest.approx), with an inline comment citing issue #704, the CPython 3.12 Neumaier-sum change, and the measured 52%-of-20000-random-grids divergence rate so a future tidier cannot mistake it for a contrived test (critic C4); (3) .agent-work/issue-704/evidence/axis_snapshot.py -- a work-area-only harness (NOT committed) that evaluates `_axis_means`, `grand_two_way_center`, `per_driver_demean`, `main_effect_margin_uncertainty`, `compare_channels_by_class` and `out_of_sample_coverage` over a FIXED adversarial grid corpus and serialises every float via float.hex(), with `--emit <path>`, `--compare <path>` (exit non-zero on ANY bit difference) and `--self-test`; (4) the emitted baseline at .agent-work/issue-704/evidence/axis_snapshot_before.json. CRITICAL (critic C1): `--self-test` must prove the harness is SENSITIVE -- monkeypatch the mean into float(np.mean(...)) and assert the comparison FAILS. A harness that cannot fail on a known-wrong implementation is not evidence, and this gate does not close without that demonstration. Re-take the compensated-vs-naive measurement on the REPO's pinned interpreter, not the agent shell's 3.12 (critic C8). Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

g2-implement.title: G2 dedup: one axis-grouping site, bit-identical output
g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. TASK: in src/physics/instrument_panel/replication.py, replace the two duplicated two-axis grouping loops with ONE private helper. Recommended shape (Candidate B of PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md, decision D3): `_axis_value_lists(grid) -> tuple[dict[object, list[float]], dict[object, list[float]], float, int]` performing a SINGLE pass over `grid.items()` that (a) appends `float(value)` to the driver's row list and the class's column list, preserving both key-insertion order and per-key value order, and (b) accumulates the grand `total` and `count` with the same running `+=` the current code uses. Then: `_axis_means` computes grand as `total / count if count else 0.0` (the literal expression it uses today) and each axis mean via an explicit sequential loop over the value list -- NOT builtins.sum, NOT np.mean, NOT statistics.fmean/mean (decision D4); `main_effect_margin_uncertainty` drops its own loop and consumes the helper's two dicts directly, feeding `_main_effect_se` the SAME lists in the SAME order. Add a comment at the helper stating WHY the mean is a naive loop -- CPython>=3.12 builtins.sum is Neumaier-compensated and numpy.mean is pairwise; either changes results on ~52%/~42% of randomized ragged grids and breaks the byte-identical contract of issue #704. This comment is the GUARANTEED home for that rationale; the packet decision bullet is only a proposal carried to reconcile (critic C5). Keep the diff minimal: one new private helper (plus, if needed, one tiny `_mean_in_order`), two rewritten function bodies, one comment. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.
